_comment: servosity is a SPECIAL case: it is engine-swapped from the servosity-msp mint via a staging strip + de-msp rename ritual that is RE-APPLIED on every reprint, so most of its divergence from a stock print is re-derived, not lost. These entries pin the load-bearing engine-swap invariants so a NAIVE reprint (one that bypassed the ritual) is caught. NOTE: a full reprint-diff would surface more; this records the auth/identity invariants that matter most. Issue #78 (bare SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN lacked the required 'Token ' DRF auth-scheme prefix -> HTTP 403 on every data endpoint) is FIXED in AuthHeader() and pinned below; the servosity-msp engine still emits a bare token, so a reprint that bypassed re-applying this prefix would reintroduce the bug. 2026-08-17 (4.30.3 reprint): the admin-only-endpoints entry gained asserts for two surfaces the 4.24.0 ledger did not cover - cli/internal/cli/channel_workflow.go (the workflow sync resource list) and cli/internal/cli/root_test.go (the 4.30 declared-API-surface conformance test, which FAILS the build if a declared path has no Cobra command). The 4.30.3 reprint reintroduced the endpoints on both and the ledger did not catch them; they are pinned now.

handfixes.summary: MSP-token auth (SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN env var -> ServosityMspToken -> AuthHeader) is hand-wired by the engine swap
handfixes.why: The servosity-msp engine adds an MSP partner-token auth path the stock print does not have. The env-var wiring and config field are re-applied by the de-msp ritual; a naive reprint that bypassed the ritual would drop them and break authentication.

handfixes.summary: AuthHeader() prepends the DRF 'Token ' scheme to the MSP partner token (issue #78)
handfixes.why: The Servosity API authenticates the MSP partner token via Django REST Framework's TokenAuthentication, which requires the 'Token ' scheme on the Authorization header; a bare value 403s on every data endpoint. The stock servosity-msp engine emits the token verbatim, so the de-msp ritual must re-apply this scheme prefix on every reprint or the bug returns. hasAuthScheme tolerates an already-prefixed value for backward compatibility with the SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN='Token <t>' workaround.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press supports x-prefix on an apiKey header securityScheme (docs/SPEC-EXTENSIONS.md), which would make the press emit the 'Token ' scheme natively and retire this hand-fix. NOT adopted yet: the generated applyAuthFormat path would prepend unconditionally, double-prefixing every user who set SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN='Token <t>' per the old workaround. Adopt only together with a stripAuthScheme-equivalent normalization upstream, and only with a live-tenant retest.

handfixes.summary: issues archived (/issues/archived/) and issues ignored (/issues/ignored/) are stripped from EVERY surface (CLI, MCP code-orch and context, sync, store, workflow resource list, declared-surface conformance test) because they are admin-scoped and 403 for the reseller-scoped partner token this connector ships (PR #178)
handfixes.why: These two GET endpoints are generated from the OpenAPI spec and admin-only; the partner SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN gets HTTP 403. A naive reprint regenerates them on every surface (the CLI command files, the MCP code-orch endpoint table agents drive via servosity-msp_search/_execute, the MCP context taxonomy agents use for discovery, the sync resource map + store PK map, the workflow sync resource list, and - since press 4.30 - the declared-API-surface conformance test in root_test.go, which fails the build when a declared path has no Cobra command). The de-msp ritual must re-strip all of them; these not_contains asserts fail CI if any surface reintroduced them. Admin functionality lives in Servosity's separate internal admin CLI (admin-token-scoped) instead. See docs/reprint-survival.md.

handfixes.summary: current-user API-token retrieval is explicit human-only CLI behavior and is excluded from MCP, sync, archive, response caches, and the local search store; schema v10 purges previously mirrored copies (issue #254)
handfixes.why: The generated GET command returned a live credential through every CLI format, MCP code orchestration, default sync, workflow archive, the HTTP response cache, SQLite resources, FTS search, and arbitrary read-only MCP SQL. A reprint would restore all of those generated surfaces. The CLI now requires --reveal-token, forces live/no-cache resolution, and is mcp:hidden. MCP discovery, code orchestration, sync, and archive omit the endpoint. Store schema v10 purges known historical rows and rebuilds FTS before MCP may open an old store, while the generic persistence boundary rejects future sensitive rows. Constructor-time cache cleanup removes the old current-user response namespace for each active cache profile. Logical cleanup cannot erase old binaries, free pages, WAL files, backups, or transcripts, so the security release also requires rotation guidance.

handfixes.summary: auth set-token and auth logout write and delete the credentials store colocated with an explicit --config / SERVOSITY_MSP_CONFIG file, not just the default data-dir store (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The generated cliutil credentials layer is config-path-aware on READ (LoadCredentialsForConfigWithStatus resolves <dir-of-config>/data/credentials.toml and Load prefers it) but not on WRITE: SaveCredentials and RemoveCredentials always resolved the DEFAULT store. With --config or SERVOSITY_MSP_CONFIG set, `auth logout` printed 'Logged out. Credentials cleared.' while the sibling token stayed on disk and kept authenticating every later call, and `auth set-token` wrote the rotated token to the default store while the sibling kept serving the OLD one - a rotation the operator believes happened but did not. The fix adds SaveCredentialsForConfig / RemoveCredentialsForConfig mirroring the read-path resolution, records explicitConfigFile on Config so the write paths can honor it, routes saveCredentialsFirst/ClearTokens through them, and makes the path `auth set-token` prints follow the store it actually wrote. All four files are generated ('DO NOT EDIT'), so a reprint on an unfixed press silently restores the false-logout. Regression tests live in the hand-written cli/internal/config/config_test.go and fail without the fix.

handfixes.summary: the MCP shell-out gate refuses every flag whose usage text names a filesystem location, not just the four names the generated denylist happened to carry (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account, so any forwarded flag that names a local path lets a tool caller choose where that account reads or writes. The generated blockedDestinationFlags list covered audit-dir/o/output/receipt-file and missed --db (every local-store command), --out (qbr, qbr-all), --input (import), --notes-file / --playbook-file / --playbook-notes-file (teach, teach-playbook) and --reconcile (bill): 28 of 155 tools exposed one. Driving learnings_list with {"db": "<any path>"} created a 1.8 MB SQLite file at that path. The fix adds the missing names to the static floor AND adds isFilesystemPathFlag, a per-command rule matching the flag's USAGE text so a newly generated path flag is refused by default. Matching usage rather than name is load-bearing: this CLI ships generated API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values never touch the server filesystem, and a name-based rule would break those real API surfaces. Both files are generated, so a reprint reopens all 28 tools.

handfixes.summary: a host-changing redirect drops EVERY credential-classed header, not only Authorization (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The generated CheckRedirect deleted only Authorization on a cross-host hop while Go replayed every other header verbatim. The 4.30 surface added 26 --x-servosity-mfa flags, so X-Servosity-Mfa is a second live credential on the wire, and config.headers lets an operator put an API key in any header name they like. A 3xx from the API (open redirect or partner handoff) therefore handed those credentials to a host the operator never authenticated against. The fix adds isCredentialHeader (exact names plus a hyphen/underscore SEGMENT match on auth/token/secret/key/session/mfa/otp/signature/... so unrelated names such as X-Assignee do not trip it) and stripCredentialHeaders, called only on the cross-host branch. Same-host redirects still re-derive Authorization, so nonce-bound schemes keep working and paginated redirects do not start 401ing. client.go is generated, so a reprint restores the single-header strip.

handfixes.summary: root.go carries the transcendent Short/Long describing all 13 novel commands, not the press's generic one-liner
handfixes.why: The press emits Short/Long as "Manage servosity-msp resources via the servosity-msp API". That does two kinds of damage at once. It DROPS the discovery surface for every novel command from --help and agent-context - the 13 highlights are the whole reason this connector is more than a generated API wrapper, and an agent reading agent-context can no longer find them. And it prints the internal MINT SLUG servosity-msp where the product name belongs. Note the slug is meaningful, not noise: servosity-msp is the MSP-fleet CLI as distinct from servosity-admin, a separate CLI. The de-msp ritual does not erase that distinction - it renders it in the readable product name, which is why the restored text reads "Servosity Msp CLI - The first MSP-fleet CLI for backup". Do not scrub the MSP distinction; keep the internal slug out of user-facing prose while preserving the product identity. The module path servosity-msp-pp-cli and the SERVOSITY_MSP_* env vars stay untouched by design. Verified dropped by the 4.30.3 reprint; re-apply the transcendent block on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For servosity the manifest gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. server.json gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.
